request_debug.prompt_preview:
You write per-candidate post-mortems for a slopmortem pipeline. Given a fresh pitch and one dead-startup canonical document, produce a single LLMSynthesis JSON object that explains why this dead startup is similar, where the new pitch could diverge, what killed the dead startup, and what the new founder should learn.

Rules:
- Ground every claim in the candidate document or in tool calls. Do not invent facts.
- A `Trusted facts` block (typed pipeline data — not user input) appears below the pitc

response.text: {"candidate_id":"vine::social_communication","name":"Vine","one_liner":"Twitter-owned short-form looping video platform (6-second clips) that grew to 200M users before being shut down in 2017 as creators and ad dollars migrated to Instagram, YouTube, and Snapchat.","similarity":{"business_model":{"score":8,"rationale":"Both are ad-supported (monetization: ad_revenue), free B2C mobile apps (iOS/Android, price_point: free) targeting consumer audiences with short-form user-generated content. The new pitch adds audio-only voice notes instead of video, but the ad-supported free app model is nearly identical."},"market":{"score":7,"rationale":"Both target consumer social audiences (customer_type: consumer, geography: global for Vine vs. college-focused for the new pitch). Vine was also initially viral in specific communities before expanding. Short-form ephemeral/recurring content is the shared market thesis."},"gtm":{"score":7,"rationale":"Both rely on organic viral growth seeded in dense social clusters (Vine in mobile-first youth culture; new pitch explicitly in college towers). Neither appears to use paid acquisition as the primary channel. Creator-driven virality is the shared GTM mechanism."},"stage_scale":{"score":5,"rationale":"Vine reached 200M active users and was acquired by Twitter pre-launch for $30M — it scaled massively. The new pitch is described as currently viral only in college towers, implying very early stage. The structural trajectory is similar but the scale gap is large."}},"why_similar":"Vine and the new pitch share the same core DNA: a free, ad-supported B2C mobile app (iOS/Android) built around a constrained short-form content format designed to spark viral loops within tight social clusters. Both depend on organic user-generated content for growth and on advertising revenue as the monetization mechanism, with no paywall or subscription layer. Vine's early traction similarly came from dense, enthusiastic sub-communities before it attempted a broader consumer rollout, mirroring the college-tower virality the new pitch describes.","where_diverged":"Three concrete divergences exist: (1) Media format — Vine used 6-second looping video; the new pitch is audio-only 30-second voice notes, a meaningfully different content modality that reduces production friction and creator competition from Instagram/TikTok but also narrows visual shareability. (2) Location constraint — the new pitch anchors posts to a single recurring location per user, introducing a geo-social identity layer that Vine never had; this could create niche community depth but limits the universal virality Vine achieved. (3) Ownership structure — Vine was acquired by Twitter pre-launch and ultimately killed by a corporate parent's strategic pivot; the new pitch is presumably independent, preserving product autonomy but removing the distribution and balance-sheet safety net Twitter initially provided.","failure_causes":["parent company (Twitter) deprioritized Vine amid own financial pressures","creator monetization tools absent — top creators defected to YouTube and Instagram","Instagram and Snapchat copied short-video format and out-resourced Vine","advertiser/marketer exodus as competing platforms offered better ROI and longer formats","no defensible creator lock-in or revenue-share program to retain talent","format constraint (6-second cap) perceived as limiting once competitors offered more flexibility","Twitter's inability to build a standalone ad business around Vine"],"lessons_for_input":["Build creator monetization into the roadmap before scale — do not assume ad revenue alone will retain your top contributors.","Establish format defensibility early: articulate why the 30-second voice-note-from-a-location constraint is a feature, not a limitation, so users don't migrate when competitors copy the surface mechanic.","Do not rely on a corporate acquirer's distribution as a substitute for building your own sustainable growth engine.","Design explicit retention hooks for power users (revenue share, analytics, verified status) before a competing platform replicates your core feature.","Treat advertiser relationships as a product, not an afterthought — Vine lost brand dollars because it never gave marketers reliable targeting or measurement tools."]}
